A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the active psychotherapy style, which aimed to elicit feelings, produced the most positive responses in the interviewees, whereas the structured and the systematic exploratory styles produced less positive reactions.
the four styles are not only different from one another, but that they are also differentially effective in eliciting different types of information from the same patient.

, in a psychiatric interview, a combination of fact-oriented and feeling-orientated techniques, with an appropriate balance between the two, is most likely to elicit the maximum amount of relevant information.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a wide range of interviewing styles which are effective in eliciting different types of information.
it is possible to develop a range of interview styles which are different, yet natural and which may be effective in eliciting a range of information.
it is feasible to train interviewers to adopt a variety of styles, and to compare the effects of different styles in a controlled manner.
